scenarios.exception: shape-only: the inventory lists each runtime's own tool library (Python's allowlist disables the file ops and ships senders; Go defers 51 flat names), so only the envelope keys/types are contract.
branch: Python reports "Nothing to load" (read_file/skill_view are outside its allowlist), Go promotes both. Recorded, not compared — the branches differ by tool library.

text-only: Python converts the id with int() and lets the CPython ValueError escape ("invalid literal for int()"), Go answers with a typed argument error. Both are is_error JSON envelopes with an error key.
text-only: Python resolves the path against its session dir and reports a misleading "File not found"; Go refuses the escape explicitly. Same outcome (no bytes, plain-text refusal, is_error=false).

envelope: an oversized result spills on both sides, but Python emits a structural digest + grep hint and Go emits a bounded preview with a sampling warning. Reviewed and kept: different spillover designs, each self-consistent.

envelope: Python returns a JSON result envelope (exit_code/stdout/pid/runtime_ms/semantic_status/...), Go returns a text report (exit_code/shell_kind/stdout/stderr). The terminal output shape is the terminal lane's frozen contract; retargeting it is a terminal-lane change, not an output-shape fix.
tool-set: skill_view exists only on Go (Python answers "Unknown tool"). Both are is_error JSON envelopes.
unported: credentials is a Python-only model tool; Go answers with the explicit not_implemented envelope.
unported: sentinel_setup needs the desktop connector; Go answers with the explicit not_implemented envelope.
unported: Go has no background tool handles; the envelope points at terminal_job_logs instead.
unported: suggest_colony drives the colony popup; Go answers with the explicit not_implemented envelope.

tool-set: excel_read does not exist in Python ("Unknown tool ... Did you mean 'csv_read'?"); on Go it is a deferred name and the loop refuses it with the select: prompt. Both are actionable is_error envelopes.
